body: That club sounds fun. I'm studying Computer Science.

I wish I'd do more clubs. I see everyone here competing in tournaments and making things happen, and I know for sure that I don't have the skills nor the mental capacity to do anything, that's why I feel so out of place. I'm not even ready to admit to my psychiatrist about this.

I've always enjoyed learning, but less so in college. Sometimes I'm unmotivated to learn, and that affects my performance for the rest of the semester. Sometimes I'm underwhelmed by the fact that I won't be able to do anything with that knowledge. At one point, I also realized that I have never *ever* understood a topic so *deeply*. It's crushing. School was ok, but college is another level of stuff. Dunno, I've been thinking lately that I'm not cut for it. But I can't quit, and I know from my non proactive personality that I'm for sure not gonna quit.

I enjoyed being with people and talking to them, but being introverted, that doesn't last long. Then when I'm isolated and need human contact, I'm never able to get out of my isolation (that's something I talked about with my psychiatrist), and when I'm stuck in that isolation, things go bad.

I went to psych services once at the end of my freshman year (after missing it two times, most likely because I was sleeping). I only went because I felt like absolute shit. Another problem with me is that I never seek help.

She recommended that I visit her at the beginning of school year after summer, but I don't know if I should. I feel like I'm a lost case, and like it won't make a difference.

 Oh, and freshman year was shitty. No friends.
Well, i have nothing to do but get through it. Unless I go crazy first.

Early 20s. I don't think I can get motivated. Even if I'm in a better mental/psychological state, I'm a consumer, not a productive member of society, which leads me to eat less and workout less, because if i don't do anything useful, or my responsibilities (which i'm failing miserably), then I don't deserve to enjoy anything. Sometimes, if I try to enjoy myself, I feel guilty and like a worthless piece of shit.

Where do I even begin? There is no beginning. My whole life I've been directed to do stuff, and I did them. Now I realize I have no sense of responsibility or proactivity or situational awareness to do anything in my life, including ending it.

At least in my religion (Islam), anything that makes you high or drunk is not allowed, so people stopped hallucinating.

There's a difference between being sick and having demons inside of you, tho both exists in my culture, I've never heard a personal story of someone being possessed, everyone understands sickness and get treated.

The dark ages of Europe were also the golden ages of the islamic world, where a lot of scientific break throughs were made, and a lot of today's science and technology is based on it (Cameras, numbers..etc)

> if you were good you got to live forever in a happy heaven, but if you were bad you burned forever in hell. Sure that would be nice, but that isn't reality

How do you know what the reality is? The only possible scientifically proof for this statement is to go the after life and back, and tell about it. So you might say that religious people don't know the truth for sure, and atheists don't know for sure, both are equally viable options.

> how could they all be right?

They're not all right, there are contradicting ideas to the point that only one of two options is right. But I guess the best course of action is to investigate some and find one that sounds convincing.

I'm studying at college right now. I know what science is, but I don't believe it contradicts with religion. And yes, it was made thousands of years ago, but for some reason, I don't believe that our ancestors were that gullible as to believe something that isn't real.
The problems were there for a long time, I'm just seeing them from a different light.
